endpoint_registry.doc_quote: Successful operation returns 200 with CollectionOperationResponse (result, status, time); invalid vectors config / enum values / malformed JSON produce a 400 validation error; creating an existing collection name fails with a 409-conflict family error.
Returns 200 with the full collection config (params, hnsw_config, optimizer_config, wal_config, quantization_config) and status/points_count; missing collection returns 404.
Returns 200 with an array of {name} CollectionDescription entries.
Update collection params; 200 ok, 404 if the collection is missing, 400 on an invalid diff.
Deleting an existing collection is confirmed with 200; a non-existent collection returns 404.
Returns 200 with {result: {exists: bool}} - a missing collection is reported as result.exists=false, never as HTTP 404.
Returns 200 with optimizer status per shard; 404 for a missing collection.
Returns 200 ok (with wait=false the client gets an acknowledge-only response immediately); 400 on invalid payload / vector dimension mismatch; 404 when the collection is missing.
By default payload and vector are NOT returned - opt in with with_payload/with_vector; 200 array of Record; missing ids are simply absent from the result, not an error.
Returns 200 with the Record; 404 if the point or the collection does not exist.
Delete by filter is allowed (whole-collection wipe if the filter matches all); deleting non-existent ids is an idempotent success; 200 ok, 404 for a missing collection, 400 for an invalid filter.
Operations are executed in order; returns 200 with per-operation results; 404 for a missing collection.
exact=true (default) gives an exact count (slower); returns 200 {count}; 404 for a missing collection.
Paginates via next_page_offset in the response (null when exhausted); returns 200 {points, next_page_offset}; 404 for a missing collection.
Points OR filter must identify the targets (both null is an error); returns 200 ok, 400, 404.
Replaces the entire payload of targeted points (set semantics: keys missing from the new payload are removed); 200 ok / 400 / 404.
Removes all payload keys of the targeted points; 200 ok / 404.
Deletes only the listed keys of the targeted points; 200 ok / 400 / 404.
Updates only the specified named vectors; unspecified vectors of the point stay unchanged; 200 ok, 400 on dimension mismatch, 404 when the point or collection is missing.
Deletes the named vectors listed in vector (the unnamed default vector is deletable too); 200 ok / 404.
Returns 200 QueryResponse {result: [ScoredPoint], next_page_offset?}; 400 on an invalid query; 404 when the collection is missing.
Executes multiple queries in one call; returns 200 with a list of per-query results; 404 for a missing collection.
Grouping requires payload values for the group_by field; pagination (offset) is NOT allowed with groups; returns 200 {groups: [{id, hits}]}; 404; 400 for an invalid group_by.
Returns 200 [ScoredPoint]; 400 on dimension mismatch or an invalid vector name; 404 when the collection is missing.
Returns 200 with an array of per-search [ScoredPoint]; 400 on dimension mismatch; 404 for a missing collection.
Pagination is not available with groups; returns 200 {groups}; 400 for an invalid vector/group_by; 404 for a missing collection.
Returns 200 [ScoredPoint]; 400 when a referenced point lacks the used vector (fetched vectors must match the using-vector characteristics); 404 for a missing collection.
Returns 200 with an array of per-search results; 400 when a referenced id lacks the used vector; 404 for a missing collection.
Pagination (offset) is not available in groups APIs; returns 200 {groups: [{id, hits}]}; 404; 400 for an invalid group_by.
Returns 200 [ScoredPoint]; 400 on invalid context/pairs; 404 for a missing collection.
Returns 200 [ScoredPoint]; 400 on invalid context/pairs; 404 for a missing collection.
Returns 200 {result: {offsets_row, offsets_col, scores, ids}}; 400 on out-of-range sample/limit; 404 for a missing collection.
Returns 200 {result: {pairs_a, pairs_b, scores, ids}}; 400 on invalid input; 404 for a missing collection.
Faceting works only on a payload field with an index supporting MatchValue conditions; returns 200 {response: [FacetValueHit {value, count}]}; 404; 400 (including when no suitable index exists).
Creates a payload field index; returns 200 ok; 400 on an invalid field schema; 404 when the collection is missing.
Deleting a non-existent index succeeds (idempotent 200); deleting an index does not delete data.
Adds a new named vector to an existing collection (1.18 feature); 200 ok; 400 on invalid params or a name conflict; 404 for a missing collection.
Removes the named vector together with its data; 200 ok; 404 when the vector name or the collection is missing.
Returns 200 with a list of {alias, collection_name} across all collections.
Returns 200 with a list of {alias, collection_name}; 404 for an unknown collection.
Alias changes are ATOMIC - no collection modifications can happen between alias operations; 200 ok; 404 on create_alias of a missing collection; 404/500 on delete_alias of an unknown alias.
Returns 200 with cluster info (peer_id, raft_state, commit_index, peers); valid on single-node deployments too.
Returns 200 TelemetryData (id, app, collections, cluster, requests, memory, hardware, search_pool, quota); internal/ops-oriented.

Removing the last peer or self may break raft consensus; force bypasses the safety check; removing a peer hosting the only replica can cause data loss (by-design destructive); 200 ok; 4xx on invalid peer id.
Removes cluster metadata and restarts as a single-node cluster from local data; irrecoverable for removed peers; use only when quorum is permanently lost.
Returns 200 with CollectionClusterInfo; 404 for an unknown collection.
Async transfer initiation - 200 means accepted, not completed; shard transfers are observable via collection cluster info; 200 ok; 400 on invalid peer/shard; 404 for a missing collection.
Returns 200 with a list of shard keys and their shard counts; 404 for a missing collection.
Requires a collection created with sharding_method=custom; existing data is NOT retro-sharded; 200 ok; 400 on wrong sharding method or a duplicate key; 404 for a missing collection.

Creates a full snapshot of all shards of the collection; returns 200 SnapshotDescription; 404 for a missing collection.

Irreversible delete; 200 ok; 404 when missing.

type_constraints.description: vectors config: VectorParams requires size (uint64) and distance; distance is a strict enum [Cosine, Euclid, Dot, Manhattan]
type_constraints.assertion: vectors.distance IN {Cosine, Euclid, Dot, Manhattan}; VectorParams.required = [size, distance]; vectors.size is an unsigned integer (uint64)

type_constraints.description: sparse vector params: sparse_vectors is a map of name to SparseVectorParams; sparse vector distance is always Dot and is not user-settable [DOC vectors]
type_constraints.assertion: sparse vector distance IS Dot (not user-settable); sparse_vectors configuration is a map of vector-name to SparseVectorParams

type_constraints.description: sharding_method domain per the versioned OpenAPI: ShardingMethod enum [auto, custom] (snake_case wire values; the concept-doc prose variant 'hash_slot' is not part of the v1.18.0 spec)
type_constraints.assertion: sharding_method IN {auto, custom} (versioned spec ShardingMethod enum; wire values are lowercase snake_case)

type_constraints.description: quantization_config domain: Scalar quantization {type: int8} | Product {compression enum [x4, x8, x16, x32, x64]} | Binary {encoding enum [one_bit, two_bits, one_and_half_bits]}; null disables quantization
type_constraints.assertion: quantization_config type domain: ScalarQuantization.type = int8; ProductQuantization.compression IN {x4, x8, x16, x32, x64}; BinaryQuantization.encoding IN {one_bit, two_bits, one_and_half_bits}

type_constraints.description: datatype enum [float32, uint8, float16, turbo4]; turbo4 (4-bit) is dense-only and cannot be configured for sparse vectors [DOC vectors]
type_constraints.assertion: datatype IN {float32, uint8, float16, turbo4}; turbo4 is valid for dense vectors only

type_constraints.description: memory placement enum [cold, cached, pinned] (1.18); pinned is not supported for dense vector storage; memory replaces the deprecated on_disk / always_ram booleans [SPEC]
type_constraints.assertion: memory IN {cold, cached, pinned}; pinned is not supported for dense vector storage

type_constraints.description: PointStruct.id is a oneOf of 64-bit unsigned integer or UUID string; every request accepts a UUID string wherever a numeric id is valid [DOC manage-data/points]
type_constraints.assertion: point id type domain: uint64 integer OR uuid string (both valid in every request)

type_constraints.description: PointStruct.vector oneOf: dense float array (unnamed default vector), named object {name: [values]}, multivector arrays, sparse {indices: [uint], values: [float]}; payload is arbitrary JSON [DOC points + vectors]
type_constraints.assertion: vector field accepts dense array | named object | multivector matrix | sparse {indices, values}; payload accepts arbitrary JSON

type_constraints.description: query variant (oneOf): nearest (dense/sparse/multivector/document/image/custom, with optional mmr), recommend, discover, context, order_by, fusion (RRF/DBSF), sample (random), neartext/nearimage (inference-based, unimplemented per spec WARN) [SPEC]
type_constraints.assertion: query variant domain: nearest | recommend | discover | context | order_by | fusion | sample | neartext | nearimage (oneOf; neartext/nearimage are inference variants)

type_constraints.description: field_schema type domain: PayloadSchemaType enum [keyword, integer, float, geo, text, bool, datetime, uuid]; text tokenizer enum [prefix, whitespace, word, multilingual]
type_constraints.assertion: field_schema IN {keyword, integer, float, geo, text, bool, datetime, uuid}; text tokenizer IN {prefix, whitespace, word, multilingual}

type_constraints.description: payload values with non-trivial literal syntax: geo values are objects {lon, lat} of doubles; datetime values are RFC 3339 strings; uuid values are uuid strings; arrays must be same-type [DOC payload + filtering]
type_constraints.assertion: payload/filter literal formats: geo point = {lon, lat}; datetime = RFC 3339 string; uuid = uuid string; arrays are same-typed

type_constraints.description: body type LocksOption {write: boolean (required), error_message: string|null}
type_constraints.assertion: body LocksOption: write is a required boolean; error_message is string or null

type_constraints.description: body type QuotaConfig {enabled (boolean, default false), max_resident_memory_percent (integer|null), max_disk_usage_percent (integer|null), release_margin_percent (integer|null)}; null means the resource is not capped
type_constraints.assertion: body QuotaConfig: enabled boolean (default false); the three percent fields are integer or null (null = not capped)

type_constraints.description: response shape: ClusterStatus {peer_id (uint64), raft_state enum [Leader, Follower, Candidate, PreCandidate, Terminated], commit_index (uint64), peers map}
type_constraints.assertion: response fields: peer_id uint64; raft_state IN {Leader, Follower, Candidate, PreCandidate, Terminated}; commit_index uint64; peers map

type_constraints.description: response shape: CollectionClusterInfo {peer_id, shard_count (minimum 0), local_shards, remote_shards, shard_transfers, resharding_operations}
type_constraints.assertion: response contains peer_id, shard_count (minimum 0), local_shards, remote_shards, shard_transfers, resharding_operations
response items: SnapshotDescription with name, creation_time, size, checksum

type_constraints.description: response shape TelemetryData {id, app, collections, cluster, requests, memory, hardware, search_pool, quota}
type_constraints.assertion: response contains id, app, collections, cluster, requests, memory, hardware, search_pool, quota sections

type_constraints.description: response shape LocksOption {write: boolean, error_message: string|null}
type_constraints.assertion: response is LocksOption with write boolean and error_message (string or null)

range_constraints.description: timeout query parameter: schema minimum 1 second (seconds to wait before the operation times out)

hnsw_config at create accepts the HnswConfigDiff schema (CreateCollectionHnswConfig): m minimum 0, ef_construct minimum 4, full_scan_threshold minimum 10 (KB), max_indexing_threads minimum 0 (0 = auto), payload_m minimum 0
range_constraints.assertion: hnsw_config (create, HnswConfigDiff schema): m minimum 0; ef_construct minimum 4; full_scan_threshold minimum 10 (KB); max_indexing_threads minimum 0; payload_m minimum 0

range_constraints.description: update-time HnswConfigDiff schema minima: m >= 0, ef_construct >= 4, full_scan_threshold >= 10 (KB, diff-specific minimum), payload_m >= 0
range_constraints.assertion: HnswConfigDiff (update): m minimum 0; ef_construct minimum 4; full_scan_threshold minimum 10 (KB); payload_m minimum 0

range_constraints.description: scalar quantization quantile must lie in [0.5, 1.0]
range_constraints.assertion: ScalarQuantization quantile within the closed interval [0.5, 1.0]

range_constraints.description: optimizers_config at create accepts the OptimizersConfigDiff schema (bounds identical to PATCH update): deleted_threshold in [0, 1], vacuum_min_vector_number minimum 100, max_segment_size minimum 1 (KB), memmap_threshold minimum 0, indexing_threshold minimum 0 (KB)
range_constraints.assertion: optimizers_config bounds: deleted_threshold within [0, 1]; vacuum_min_vector_number minimum 100; max_segment_size minimum 1 KB; memmap_threshold minimum 0; indexing_threshold minimum 0 KB

range_constraints.description: optimizer config numeric bounds (update diff): deleted_threshold in [0, 1], vacuum_min_vector_number minimum 100, max_segment_size minimum 1 (KB), memmap_threshold minimum 0, indexing_threshold minimum 0 (KB)
range_constraints.assertion: optimizers_config (diff) bounds: deleted_threshold within [0, 1]; vacuum_min_vector_number minimum 100; max_segment_size minimum 1 KB; memmap_threshold minimum 0; indexing_threshold minimum 0 KB

range_constraints.description: wal_config at create accepts the WalConfigDiff schema: wal_capacity_mb minimum 1 (resolved default 32), wal_segments_ahead minimum 0, wal_retain_closed minimum 0 (resolved default 1)
range_constraints.assertion: wal_config (create, WalConfigDiff schema): wal_capacity_mb minimum 1; wal_segments_ahead minimum 0; wal_retain_closed minimum 0

range_constraints.description: strict_mode max_resident_memory_percent bounded to [1, 100]; deprecated in 1.18 (removal scheduled 1.21), superseded by the node-wide quota config PUT /quotas
sparse vector non-zero value count is bounded by the unsigned 32-bit range [DOC vectors]
range_constraints.assertion: sparse vector non-zero value count must not exceed the unsigned 32-bit range

range_constraints.description: scroll limit (page size) schema minimum 1, default 10
universal query pagination bounds: limit minimum 1 (default 10); offset minimum 0 (default 0); large offsets may cause performance issues [DOC search]
SearchParams: hnsw_ef minimum 1; exact default false; indexed_only default false; acorn disabled by default with acorn_scale in [0.0, 1.0] (default 0.4) [DOC search]
legacy search limit is required with schema minimum 1; offset minimum 0
recommend request pagination bounds: limit required with minimum 1; offset minimum 0
group query bounds: group_size minimum 1 (default 3, max points per group); limit minimum 1 (default 10, max amount of groups)
group search bounds: group_size minimum 1; limit minimum 1 (max amount of groups)
recommend groups bounds: group_size minimum 1; limit minimum 1
matrix offsets bounds per the v-1-18-x spec: sample minimum 2 (default 10, points to select); limit minimum 1 (default 3, neighbours per sample); the spec declares no maximum bounds
matrix pairs bounds per the v-1-18-x spec: sample minimum 2 (default 10); limit minimum 1 (default 3); the spec declares no maximum bounds
facet limit minimum 1 (default 10); the v-1-18-x spec documents no maximum
quota percent bounds: max_resident_memory_percent and max_disk_usage_percent within [1, 100]; release_margin_percent within [0, 100]; null means the resource is not capped
range_constraints.assertion: max_resident_memory_percent within [1, 100]; max_disk_usage_percent within [1, 100]; release_margin_percent within [0, 100] (each nullable)

range_constraints.description: cluster telemetry timeout query parameter: default 60, minimum 1

state_constraints.description: 1.18 allows changing index/quantization/disk configuration post-create through update; vector-space-defining properties (size/distance of an existing named vector) cannot be altered through update [DOC collections]
state_constraints.assertion: after creation, size/distance of an existing (named) vector cannot be changed via PATCH update; index/quantization/disk config can

state_constraints.description: default upsert = insert-or-update by id; update_mode variants exist (1.18): insert_only (existing points are not updated), update_only (missing points are not inserted); update_filter restricts the targets [SPEC]
state_constraints.assertion: upsert default semantics: insert new points and update existing ones by id; update_mode=insert_only skips existing ids; update_mode=update_only skips missing ids

state_constraints.description: delete by filter is allowed and matches all points when the filter is empty/matches everything; deleting non-existent ids is an idempotent success
state_constraints.assertion: delete of non-existent point ids returns success (idempotent); filter-based delete removes every matching point (all points when the filter matches all)

state_constraints.description: operations are executed in order inside one batch request; batchable ops: upsert, update_vectors, delete_vectors, set_payload, overwrite_payload, delete_payload, clear_payload, delete_points [DOC points]
state_constraints.assertion: batch operations are applied sequentially in the order given; each operation reports its own result

state_constraints.description: pagination is driven by the response's next_page_offset field; passing it as offset continues the scroll; pagination is exhausted when next_page_offset is null
state_constraints.assertion: scroll returns next_page_offset to continue; null next_page_offset means the scroll is exhausted

state_constraints.description: payload-based order_by REQUIRES a payload index supporting ranges on that field, otherwise the request is rejected [DOC points]
state_constraints.assertion: order_by on a payload field is rejected unless a range-capable payload index exists on that field

state_constraints.description: points OR filter must identify the targets; both absent (null) is an error (spec: either a points list or a filter)
state_constraints.assertion: payload targets: exactly one of points-list or filter must identify targets; both null is rejected

state_constraints.description: overwrite replaces the ENTIRE payload of the targeted points (set semantics: keys missing from the new payload are removed)
state_constraints.assertion: after overwrite the point payload equals the provided payload; previously stored keys absent from the new payload are removed

state_constraints.description: clear removes all payload keys of the targeted points
state_constraints.assertion: after clear, targeted points carry no payload keys

state_constraints.description: delete removes only the listed keys; all other payload keys stay untouched
state_constraints.assertion: only the listed payload keys are removed; unlisted keys persist

state_constraints.description: update affects only the specified named vectors of each point; vectors not listed in the request stay unchanged [DOC points]
state_constraints.assertion: updating vectors of a point changes only the named vectors given; the point's other vectors remain unchanged

state_constraints.description: delete removes the named vectors listed in the vector parameter; the unnamed default vector is deletable too; 200 ok / 404
state_constraints.assertion: delete_vectors removes exactly the named vectors listed (the unnamed default vector included) from the targeted points

state_constraints.description: by-id lookup (query = point id) fetches the stored vector of that point; fetched vectors must match the characteristics of the using vector, otherwise an error is returned [DOC search]
state_constraints.assertion: by-id query uses the referenced point's stored vector; if it does not match the using vector characteristics the request errors

state_constraints.description: the groups query API does not allow offset (pagination); the same restriction applies to the legacy search/recommend groups variants [DOC search]

state_constraints.description: facet works only on a payload field that has an index supporting MatchValue conditions (e.g. keyword index); without a suitable index the request fails with 400 [DOC payload]

state_constraints.description: adds a new named vector space to an existing collection (1.18 feature); name conflicts or invalid params return 400

state_constraints.description: removes the named vector space together with its stored data; 404 when the vector name or collection is missing
state_constraints.assertion: deleting a named vector removes the vector space and its data from the collection

state_constraints.description: alias changes are ATOMIC: no collection modifications can happen between the alias operations of one request [SPEC description]
state_constraints.assertion: alias operations in one request are applied atomically - no intermediate state is observable and no collection modification can interleave

state_constraints.description: creating a shard key requires a collection created with sharding_method=custom; existing data is NOT retro-sharded onto the new key
state_constraints.assertion: shard keys can only be created on custom-sharded collections; points written before key creation are not retro-sharded

state_constraints.description: deleting a shard key that still holds data fails; the key must be emptied (points deleted) first
state_constraints.assertion: a shard key holding points cannot be deleted; it must be emptied first

state_constraints.description: removing the last peer or self may break raft consensus; force bypasses the safety check; removing a peer hosting the only replica can cause data loss (by-design destructive)
state_constraints.assertion: peer removal is destructive by design: force=true bypasses safety checks, and removal of a peer holding the only replica can lose data; a 200 does not guarantee consensus survival

state_constraints.description: recover removes the cluster metadata of the current peer and restarts it as a single-node cluster from local data; the operation is irrecoverable for removed peers and is meant for permanently-lost quorum
state_constraints.assertion: cluster recovery resets the peer to a single-node cluster from local data; it is destructive for cluster membership state

state_constraints.description: these operations initiate asynchronous transfers - HTTP 200 means the operation was accepted, not completed; progress is observable through the collection cluster info endpoint
state_constraints.assertion: shard move/replicate operations return 200 on acceptance; completion is asynchronous and observable via cluster info (shard_transfers)

state_constraints.description: recovering from an uploaded snapshot replaces the whole collection data with the archive content
state_constraints.assertion: snapshot upload recovery replaces the entire collection content from the archive

state_constraints.description: recovering a shard from an uploaded snapshot replaces the shard data; priority=replica keeps existing data where it conflicts
state_constraints.assertion: shard snapshot upload replaces shard data; with priority=replica existing data is kept on conflict

state_constraints.description: write=true blocks ALL mutation APIs, returning the configured error_message on any write attempt; designed for maintenance windows; write=false releases the lock
state_constraints.assertion: with write=true every mutation request is refused with the configured error_message until the lock is released (write=false)

state_constraints.description: limits are enforced only while enabled=true; in v1.18 this node-wide config supersedes the deprecated collection-level strict_mode max_resident_memory_percent
state_constraints.assertion: quota limits are enforced only when enabled=true; node-wide quotas supersede the deprecated strict-mode memory percent field

behavioral_contracts.description: a successfully created collection is immediately listable, gettable and reported as existing
behavioral_contracts.scenario: PUT /collections/{c} with a valid config returns 200 -> GET /collections -> GET /collections/{c} -> GET /collections/{c}/exists
behavioral_contracts.expected_behavior: after a 200 create, the name appears in the collections list, details are retrievable (status may be yellow/grey while indexing) and exists reports result.exists=true

behavioral_contracts.description: a successfully deleted collection disappears from listing and direct access returns 404
behavioral_contracts.expected_behavior: after a 200 delete, the list no longer contains the name, details access returns 404 and exists reports result.exists=false

behavioral_contracts.description: with wait=true an upsert is searchable before the response is returned
behavioral_contracts.scenario: PUT points (wait=true) -> scroll / batch-get / query / count the same points
behavioral_contracts.expected_behavior: after a 200 upsert with wait=true the written points are immediately visible to reads (scroll/get/query/count reflect the upserted vectors and payload)

behavioral_contracts.description: points deleted by id or filter (wait=true) are no longer returned by reads
behavioral_contracts.scenario: upsert points -> delete by ids and by filter (wait=true) -> batch-get / single get / scroll / query
behavioral_contracts.expected_behavior: after a 200 delete the deleted ids are absent from batch-get results, single get of a deleted id returns 404, and filtered scroll/search no longer return the deleted points

behavioral_contracts.description: payload overwrite replaces the whole payload of the targeted points instead of merging
behavioral_contracts.scenario: set payload keys {a,b} -> PUT payload+overwrite with {c} (wait=true) -> GET the points with payload
behavioral_contracts.expected_behavior: after overwrite the record payload equals exactly {c}; the previously stored keys {a,b} are removed (set semantics, not merge)

behavioral_contracts.description: alias operations in one request are applied atomically - no intermediate state is observable
behavioral_contracts.scenario: create collections A and B with alias 'live' on A -> POST /collections/aliases with rename_alias 'live' from A to B -> concurrent/sequential reads through alias 'live'
behavioral_contracts.expected_behavior: after a 200 the alias resolves to the new target; during and after the atomic batch no collection modification can interleave between alias operations (alias changes are ATOMIC per the spec description)

state_invariants.description: after a successful create the collection is queryable
state_invariants.assertion: created collection appears in the collections list and details; exists result.exists=true; queries against the name return 200

state_invariants.description: after a successful delete the collection must not exist
state_invariants.assertion: deleted collection is absent from the list; details access returns 404; exists reports result.exists=false

state_invariants.description: after inserting N points (wait=true) the exact count reflects N
state_invariants.assertion: upserting N points with wait=true then counting with exact=true returns count=N (for the whole collection or the matching filter)

state_invariants.description: after a successful point delete (wait=true) the point is not retrievable
state_invariants.assertion: deleted point ids are absent from batch-get results and filtered scrolls/searches; a single get of a deleted id returns 404

state_invariants.description: after a payload overwrite the stored payload equals exactly the provided payload
state_invariants.assertion: payload+overwrite (wait=true) leaves the targeted points with exactly the provided payload keys/values; keys absent from the request are removed

state_invariants.description: creating and deleting a payload index does not alter point data
state_invariants.assertion: index creation/deletion changes only the payload index (payload_schema); the stored points and their payload remain unchanged

state_invariants.description: while the write lock is set, all mutation APIs are refused
state_invariants.assertion: with write=true, mutation requests are refused with the configured error_message until the lock is released with write=false

data_types.name: PointId (ExtendedPointId)
data_types.description: oneOf 64-bit unsigned integer | UUID string; in every request a UUID string can be used instead of a numeric ID [DOC manage-data/points]

data_types.name: Dense vector
data_types.description: fixed-length array of floats (default float32); dimension must match the collection's configured size; Cosine distance auto-normalizes vectors on upload [DOC manage-data/collections]

data_types.name: Datatype enum
data_types.description: float32 (default) | float16 | uint8 | turbo4; uint8 dense vectors hold integers in range 0-255; turbo4 is 4-bit (TurboQuant), dense-only, cannot be configured for sparse vectors [DOC manage-data/vectors]

data_types.name: Sparse vector
data_types.description: {indices: [uint], values: [float]} - no fixed length, dynamically allocated; non-zero values limited to u32 range (4294967295); distance is always Dot (not user-settable) [DOC manage-data/vectors]

data_types.name: Multivector
data_types.description: matrix of same-shaped dense vectors; fixed length (dim) per row, variable count per point; requires multivector_config with comparator (enum: max_sim); MaxSim returns a single combined score per point [DOC manage-data/vectors]

data_types.name: Named vectors
data_types.description: multiple vectors per point keyed by name; each has its own size/distance/datatype; `using` selects which vector a query targets [DOC manage-data/vectors + search/search]

data_types.name: Payload JSON types (filterable)
data_types.description: integer (64-bit, i64 bounds), float (64-bit), bool, keyword (string), geo ({lon, lat} doubles), datetime (RFC 3339), uuid; arrays of same-type values supported - filter succeeds if at least one value matches [DOC manage-data/payload]

data_types.name: Filter
data_types.description: {should?, min_should?, must?, must_not?} - clauses recursively nestable to express arbitrary boolean expressions [DOC search/filtering]

data_types.name: Condition
data_types.description: oneOf: FieldCondition {key, match|range|geo_bounding_box|geo_radius|geo_polygon|values_count|is_empty|is_null}, is_empty, is_null, has_id ([PointId]), has_vector (named-vector presence), slice {slice: {of, total}}, nested {key, filter}, raw Filter (recursion) [DOC search/filtering]

data_types.name: Match
data_types.description: oneOf: value (string|int64|bool), text, text_any, phrase, prefix (byte-wise, case-sensitive), any (IN), except (NOR) [DOC search/filtering]

data_types.name: Range condition
data_types.description: {lt?, gt?, gte?, lte?} numbers; datetime ranges support RFC 3339 values [DOC search/filtering]

data_types.name: Geo conditions
data_types.description: GeoBoundingBox {top_left:{lon,lat}, bottom_right:{lon,lat}}; GeoRadius {center:{lon,lat}, radius in meters}; GeoPolygon {exterior:{points:[GeoPoint]}, interiors?} [DOC search/filtering]

data_types.name: ValuesCount
data_types.description: {lt?, gt?, gte?, lte?} each min 0 - matches arrays by element count [DOC search/filtering]

data_types.name: is_empty / is_null
data_types.description: is_empty matches a field that is missing OR null OR []; is_null matches a field that exists with null value; NULL cannot be tested via match [DOC search/filtering]

data_types.name: nested condition
data_types.description: key points to an array of objects ("data" or "data[]"); filter applies per array element; the parent point matches if at least one element matches; has_id and slice are NOT supported inside nested - place them in an adjacent must clause [DOC search/filtering]

data_types.name: Dot-notation field access
data_types.description: nested object access via "country.name"; arrays via "diet[].food" [DOC search/filtering]

data_types.name: SearchParams
data_types.description: hnsw_ef (min 1), exact (default false), quantization {rescore, oversampling}, indexed_only (default false), acorn {acorn_scale 0.0-1.0, default 0.4, disabled by default}, idf (global|local) [DOC search/search]

data_types.name: WriteOrderingType
data_types.description: weak | medium | strong (weak default; weak may reorder writes)

data_types.name: ReadConsistencyType
data_types.description: majority | quorum | all, or an integer N (number of replicas queried)

data_types.name: Memory placement enum
data_types.description: cold | cached | pinned (1.18) - replaces deprecated on_disk / always_ram booleans; pinned is not supported for dense vector storage (VectorParams.memory note) [SPEC]
